title: Inverse & composite functions
examples: How do I find the inverse function if it has a square root?
What happens to the domain when I find the inverse?
Can you show me an example of composing two different types of functions?

explain.say: Today we will look at two special ideas about functions. We will learn about composite functions and inverse functions. These ideas help us understand functions better.
A composite function means we use one function inside another function. We write this as f of g of x, or fg(x). We simply substitute the whole g(x) into the place of x in the f(x) function.
For example, if f(x) is x squared plus one, and g(x) is x plus two. Then fg(x) is (x plus two) squared plus one. We replaced x in f with g(x).

Next we look at the inverse function, which is written as f inverse of x, or f⁻¹(x). The inverse function essentially reverses what the original function did. If f takes x to y, then f⁻¹ takes y back to x.

items: Original: f(x) takes x to y
Inverse: f⁻¹(x) takes y back to x

explain.say: To find the inverse, we swap x and y in the original equation, and then we solve the new equation for y. For example, if f(x) is x plus three, then f⁻¹(x) is x minus three. We swapped x and y and then solved.

draw.text: Swap x and y, then solve.

faq.q: What does it mean to swap the domain and range when finding the inverse?
faq.a: It means that the set of all possible inputs becomes the set of all possible outputs, and vice versa. The domain of f becomes the range of f⁻¹, and the range of f becomes the domain of f⁻¹.
asks: How does the domain change for the inverse?
Do the domain and range switch places?

faq.q: Can I just swap x and y in the equation to find the inverse?
faq.a: Swapping x and y is the first step, but you must always solve the resulting equation for y to find the correct inverse function. Doing only the swap is not enough.
asks: Is swapping x and y the whole process?
What is the final step after swapping x and y?

faq.q: Does the order matter when I find fg(x) and gf(x)?
faq.a: Yes, the order matters a lot. fg(x) means you do g first, then f on the result. gf(x) means you do f first, then g on that result. They usually give different answers.
asks: Is fg(x) the same as gf(x)?
Which one should I calculate first?

faq.q: If a function is its own inverse, what does that mean?
faq.a: It means that when you calculate the inverse function, you get the exact same function back. In this case, f⁻¹(x) is equal to f(x).
asks: How do I know if a function is its own inverse?

faq.q: What is the simplest way to check if two functions are inverses?
faq.a: You can check by multiplying the two functions together. If the result is always one, then they are inverses of each other. This is called the identity check.
asks: How do I check if two functions are inverses?
What should the product of f(x) and f⁻¹(x) be?

facts: The composite function fg(x) means applying g first, then f.
The inverse function f⁻¹(x) reverses the action of f(x).
When finding the inverse, the domain of the original function becomes the range of the inverse.
If f(x) = x plus 5, then f⁻¹(x) = x minus 5.

quiz.say: If f(x) is 2x and g(x) is x plus 3, what is fg(x)?
quiz.why: You substitute the entire g(x) into f(x), so you get 2 times (x plus 3).

wrong.0: This mistake incorrectly squares the entire g(x) term instead of just multiplying.
wrong.2: This mistake happens if you only multiply the 2 by the x, forgetting the 3.
wrong.3: This mistake might happen if you incorrectly square the entire g(x) term.

quiz.say: If f(x) is x squared minus 1, what is f⁻¹(x) after swapping and solving?
quiz.why: Swapping x and y gives y = x squared minus 1. Solving for y gives y = sqrt(x + 1).

wrong.0: This is the original function f(x) and does not represent the inverse.
wrong.1: This mistake incorrectly treats the inverse as a reciprocal function.
wrong.3: This mistake results from incorrectly solving the equation after swapping x and y.

quiz.say: If f(x) = x + 4 and g(x) = x minus 1, what is gf(x)?
quiz.why: We calculate g(f(x)), meaning we plug the entire f(x) into g(x), so we get (x + 4) minus 1.

wrong.1: This mistake incorrectly subtracts 4 from x instead of adding it first.
wrong.2: This mistake incorrectly squares the x term from f(x) when calculating g(f(x)).
wrong.3: This mistake incorrectly subtracts the entire g(x) expression instead of substituting it.
